strengths: CRAFT benchmark addresses real problem: demonstrates near-zero exposure rates (0-1.8%) vs 8-76% for existing benchmarks, solving data contamination issue
Sustainable benchmark design using real continuously-updated official data via APIs enables long-term utility unlike static datasets
Comprehensive evaluation metrics including novel composite reasoning portability that tests integration of multiple edits
Thorough experimental validation: evaluates six methods, includes ablation study (Table 6), and demonstrates generalization to traditional benchmarks (Table 9)
KEDAS achieves strong balanced performance across all metrics with parameter-efficient LoRA-based design (2 hour training time)
Well-structured presentation with clear motivation for each component and reproducible experiments with full hyperparameter details
weaknesses: CRAFT scope is limited to Chinese language and two domains (statistics/finance), significantly limiting benchmark's immediate utility and generalizability claims
Composite reasoning portability limited to 2-hop reasoning—relatively simple and doesn't test complex knowledge integration
KEDAS method is incremental over LTE (Jiang et al., 2024): components (LoRA, retrieval, filtering, routing) are established; combining them does not constitute novel contribution
Diverse edit augmentation strategy (declarative/aliased forms) is manually designed for CRAFT and appears dataset-specific, undermining claims of universal methodology
Experimental evaluation limited to single LLM (Llama-3.1-8B) for main results; while exposure computed across five models, generalization across model families is unsubstantiated

Critical filter component suffers from limited generalization (acknowledged for Finance subset in ablation); false negative issues cause edit success degradation vs IKE, but root causes are not analyzed
Edit augmentation relies on external GPT-4o-mini API, creating dependency and unclear quality assessment of generated augmentations
Shallow error analysis: no investigation into why existing methods fail beyond zero exposure, no breakdown of failure modes by edit type or reasoning complexity
Inconsistent experimental details: IKE evaluated with 8-shot 'due to limited resources', raising fairness concerns in baseline comparison
High variance in baseline performance across metrics (e.g., EREN: 91.68 temporal vs 22.12 edit success) remains unexplained; no analysis of metric trade-offs

strengths: Compelling exposure analysis revealing significant data contamination in existing knowledge editing datasets, validating the need for CRAFT with ~0% exposure vs. 20-50% for existing datasets
Comprehensive evaluation framework with novel metrics (composite reasoning portability, alias portability, temporal/common-sense locality) providing nuanced assessment beyond edit success
Elegant use of official APIs for automatic real-time dataset updates, creating a scalable, reproducible methodology applicable to other domains
Rigorous experimental evaluation comparing 7 methods across two benchmarks with ablation studies demonstrating all KEDAS components contribute meaningfully
Strong balanced empirical results: ~99-100% edit success with 100% locality and competitive portability, addressing a core challenge in knowledge editing
Detailed reproducibility information: implementation details, hyperparameters, prompt templates, and promised code/data availability
weaknesses: Severely limited generalization: CRAFT restricted to Chinese statistics/finance only; claimed 'universal methodology' is overstated since augmentation strategies are manually designed for specific domain. Only 12 months of data collected so far—insufficient to demonstrate true long-term evolution

Limited methodological novelty in KEDAS: core components borrowed from prior work (LoRA from Hu et al. 2022, inference-time retrieval from EREN, alignment from LTE). Diverse edit augmentation is simple QA-to-declarative conversion via gpt-4o-mini API; filter is standard BERT binary classifier; self-adaptive inference is binary switching logic

Critical dependence on filter quality acknowledged but inadequately addressed: Ltemporal drops to 62.50% on QWEN2.5/CRAFT-Finance; ablation shows locality collapses to 5-27% without filter. Simplistic filter training (Appendix D) uses binary 0/1 labels without accounting for semantic similarity gradients

Evaluation limitations undermine confidence: (1) small test set (1,000 instances total), (2) no statistical significance testing or error bars despite 1-2 point differences between methods, (3) unfair baseline comparisons—different methods designed for different settings (single vs. sequential); LTE also uses alignment so improvements may reflect domain design, not methodology

Incomplete baseline coverage: MEMIT, AlphaEdit, MEND, SERAC, RECIPE excluded from main experiments due to compatibility/cost issues, weakening comprehensiveness. Appendix I results on Llama-2 partially mitigate but don't address main paper

Technical concerns: (1) Binary switching in Eq. 14 is crude, (2) External API dependency for augmentation introduces cost and unreliability, (3) No analysis of failure cases, conflicting edits, or circular dependencies, (4) No statistical analysis of variance across runs, (5) Model evaluation limited to 8B parameters

strengths: CRAFT dataset effectively addresses real problem of data contamination in static knowledge editing benchmarks with near-zero exposure rates (0-1.8% vs 22-76% for existing datasets)
Comprehensive evaluation framework with five well-motivated dimensions (temporal/common-sense locality, composite/alias portability) provides deeper assessment than prior work
Automatically updatable dataset using public APIs enables genuine real-time evolution, unlike Wikipedia-based alternatives
KEDAS achieves consistent, balanced performance across all metrics on both CRAFT and KnowEdit with strong empirical results
Thorough experimental evaluation comparing 6 baseline methods on both new and established datasets with ablation studies
Well-structured presentation with reproducibility commitments and detailed implementation appendices
weaknesses: KEDAS exhibits limited methodological novelty—components (LoRA alignment, retrieval-based editing, filtering) are well-established; paper explicitly borrows from EREN and LTE; novelty is primarily combinatorial
Critical single-point-of-failure: KEDAS heavily depends on filter quality with acknowledged poor generalization (Ltemporal drops to 62.50% on CRAFT-Finance); no robust fallback mechanisms analyzed
Dataset scope severely limited to Chinese language and two narrow domains (statistics/finance); generalization to multilingual scenarios and other knowledge domains unvalidated

Questionable evaluation design: suspiciously perfect 100% locality scores on CRAFT-Statistics suggest insufficient evaluation challenge; small test set (1,000 instances) raises statistical power concerns
Significant experimental gaps: multiple baselines (MEMIT, AlphaEdit, MEND, SERAC) excluded due to compatibility issues; limited LM coverage with only Llama-3.1 and Qwen2.5 on CRAFT

Exposure measurement uses only direct prompting (indirect methodology); doesn't fully distinguish between memorization and reasoning; filter training uses overly simplistic binary relevance classification
Filter generalization unexamined: trained only on CRAFT training set; performance on other knowledge editing datasets or domains remains unclear
Augmentation method requires external gpt-4o-mini API dependency and is specifically tailored to financial/statistical data; transferability to general knowledge editing questionable
